# Exact witness optimization for Clifford verifiers with a conjunction output test

Problem: TOP-30006695  
Claim type: Partial result  
Author: /root/hundred_algorithms

**Exact scope.** For an explicitly encoded unitary Clifford verifier with ancillas initialized to zero, arbitrary quantum witnesses and acceptance iff specified output qubits are all zero, the maximum witness acceptance is exactly zero or a computable power of1/2, found in polynomial bit time. Hence this QMA verifier subclass has a classical polynomial-time decision procedure; arbitrary verifier postprocessing/non-Clifford gates are excluded.

Let U be a Clifford circuit on w witness qubits and a ancillas initialized to|0^a>. It is explicitly given using H,S,CNOT and Pauli gates, with addressed wires. Fix k distinct output wires and accept exactly on their simultaneous computational-basis outcome0. The witness may be an arbitrary mixed/entangled state on its w qubits; it is not restricted to a stabilizer state. No intermediate adaptive measurement, magic-state ancilla or arbitrary Boolean predicate on measured outputs is allowed in this scope.

For each tested output wire define P_j=U^*Z_jU. These are independent commuting Hermitian Pauli operators. Their joint acceptance projector is
\[
 U^*\Pi_{0^k}U=2^{-k}\sum_{s\in\mathbb F_2^k}P(s),\qquad
 P(s)=\prod_jP_j^{s_j}.                                  \tag{9}
\]
Pauli conjugation through every Clifford gate is exact and uses binary X/Z labels plus a phase modulo4. This is the standard stabilizer representation; signs must be retained, not discarded.

Compress(9) against the zero ancillas to obtain the witness acceptance operator M. A Pauli product has nonzero ancilla expectation iff its ancilla tensor factors are all I or Z; any X or Y gives zero. Let H be the kernel of the linear map taking s to the ancilla X-component of P(s), and h=dim H. This is an ordinary binary nullspace computation. For s in H let R(s) be its signed witness Pauli after removing ancilla I/Z factors. Since the removed factors commute and have expectation+1 on|0^a>,
\[
 R(s+t)=R(s)R(t),\qquad
 M=2^{h-k}\left(2^{-h}\sum_{s\in H}R(s)\right).           \tag{10}
\]
In particular the surviving witness Paulis commute: their full operators commute and their ancilla restrictions are diagonal commuting Paulis. Equation(10) is valid even when different s produce the same R(s).

The parenthesized operator A is an orthogonal projector. It is Hermitian, and averaging a finite group representation gives A^2=A, since each u has exactly2^h representations s+t=u. If some s gives R(s)=-I, terms pair and A=0. Otherwise the image group contains no negative identity. Choose independent unsigned Pauli generators of that image, say r of them. They are commuting signed Hermitian operators with independent binary labels, so
\[
 A=2^{-r}\prod_{i=1}^r(I+R_i)
\]
is a nonzero projector: its trace is2^{w-r}>0, since every nonidentity Pauli has trace zero and independence leaves only the empty product proportional to I. This also proves nonemptiness without searching an exponentially large Hilbert space.

Therefore
\[
 \max_\rho\operatorname{Tr}(M\rho)=
 \begin{cases}0,&-I\text{ belongs to the surviving image group},\\
 2^{h-k},&\text{otherwise}.\end{cases}                     \tag{11}
\]
A basis of H yields h signed Pauli generators. Gaussian elimination on their2w binary labels, multiplying full signed operators during row operations, detects a negative-identity relation: a zero-label row with sign-1. If none is present, the same elimination gives independent generators for the nonzero projector. Thus(11) is computable in time polynomial in the circuit's full encoded length, w+a and k, with only polynomially many bits. Wire-address reading is included; unit-cost operations on exponentially long state vectors are not used. The exact value can be represented by0 or the integer exponent k-h, rather than printing its exponentially long decimal expansion.

For the prompt's2/3-versus1/3 promise, any yes instance in this subclass must have optimum1: all nonzero alternatives below1 are at most1/2. A no instance has optimum0 or at most1/4. The value1/2 violates this promise and can receive any output. Accepting exactly when(11)equals1 therefore decides the promised subclass in P, without receiving a witness. The k=0 case gives M=I and certain acceptance, and w=0 is included.

This is a stabilizer-algebra tractable regime, distinct from an inverse-polynomial accepting-spectrum-density assumption. It can optimize a projector of exponentially small relative rank. It does not establish general QMA containment in BQP: arbitrary quantum verifiers contain non-Clifford gates and may process measurement outcomes by much more general acceptance predicates. No theorem about all procedures informally described as Clifford-assisted is claimed.
